basis: Inherited dystrophies directly affecting the corneal stroma; systemic manifestations do not characterize the umbrella.
Developmental disability defines the syndrome; cardiac defects, hearing loss and low Ig each 80-99%. Cap excludes frequent cleft palate, skeletal and skin abnormalities.
Smooth-muscle tumour growth occupies uterine veins by definition; distant cardiac extension is not required or sufficiently common.
Colorectal and upper gastrointestinal adenomatous polyposis; common retinal pigment hypertrophy generally does not impair vision. Other tumours are minority risks.
Metastatic occupation of lymph nodes; lymph nodes have no anatomical axis here. This is neither lymphoma nor a blood-cell malignancy.
Congenital cleft of the nasal ala; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis. Associated craniofacial defects are not consistently present.
Retinol transport disorder causes retinal dystrophy; comedonal acne and follicular hyperkeratosis occurred in 2/2 patients. Cardiac findings lack established frequency.
Bilateral optic nerve sheath tumours; the optic nerve is explicitly assigned to the ocular axis.
Inflammation of the reproductive glans mucosa; infection and immune-mediated disease are possible causes but do not define this mixed-etiology umbrella.
Papillary neoplasm arising in the renal pelvis, part of the urinary system.
Cerebral small-vessel disease with defining brain injury: cognitive impairment 5/5, lacunar stroke 3/3 and cerebral hemorrhage 3/6.
Corneal inflammation defines the disease; infectious and immune causes are not universal across keratitis.
Proliferative cerebral vasculopathy destroys developing brain tissue; fixed joint contractures occur in 6/7 and talipes in 5/7.
Carcinoma originates in urinary bladder epithelium; metastatic sites are not consistent defining organs.
CFTR-related cholangiopathy and hepatic injury define this liver-specific disease; other manifestations of underlying cystic fibrosis are outside its scope.
Congenital unilateral fusion of the humerus and radius directly affects the elbow skeleton and movement.
Testicular differentiation in a 46,XX individual is a reproductive developmental disorder; endocrine dysfunction is not established by the supplied phenotype.
Developmental disability and epilepsy define the disorder; strabismus reported in 2/2 assessed. Other organ findings are isolated or minor dysmorphisms; prevalence uncertain.
Malignancy originates in specialized prostatic stroma, a reproductive tissue; stromal histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Extragonadal germ-cell tumour, typically mediastinal or retroperitoneal; no specific organ within the 13 axes is established by this umbrella.
Inborn oxidative phosphorylation disorder; encephalopathy and skeletal myopathy each commonly affect at least about 30%. Cardiac and other damage varies substantially by subtype.
Photosensitive skin disease with scarring; developmental disability and microcephaly in 1/1 reported patient support neurologic involvement. Photophobia alone does not establish eye damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with low immunoglobulins defines immune dysfunction; no additional common organ damage is established.
Cerebral small-vessel disease and osteoporosis define the syndrome; lacunar strokes 7/7 and brain atrophy 5/7. Diabetes and hypertension each 1/7 are excluded.
Crossed renal ectopia is a defining urinary malformation; pelvic lipomatosis affects deep pelvic fat rather than the subcutis covered by the dermatologic axis.
